Report DescriptionENVIRONMENTAL CLIMATE CHANGE CANADA REPORTS: THE CALLER IS REPORTING AN ONGOING OVERFLOW AT THREE LOCATIONS OF THE COMBINED SEWER SYSTEM DUE TO HEAVY THUNDERSTORMS. THE LIFT STATION ON BUDD AVENUE (45.1920, -67.2716) BEGAN OVERFLOWING AT ROUGHLY 07H00 WITH AN ESTIMATED FLOW RATE OF 79.2 CUBIC METERS PER HOUR. THE DRAIN AT PARKING LOT #4 (45.1921, 67.2814) BEGAN OVERFLOWING AT ROUGHLY 08H00 WITH AN ESTIMATED FLOW RATE OF 178 CUBIC METERS PER HOUR. THE DRAIN AT CIVIC CENTER (45.1929, -67.2740) BEGAN OVERFLOWING AT ROUGHLY 07H00 WITH AN ESTIMATED FLOW RATE OF 272 CUBIC METERS PER HOUR. ALL THREE DISCHARGE INTO THE ST CROIX RIVER. THERE IS A METER ON THE DRAIN AT CIVIC CENTER. SEEING AS THE CAUSE IS THUNDERSTORMS, THE DISCHARGE IS MOSTLY RAINWATER. THERE ARE NO CONTAINMENT MEASURES IN PLACE. THE FLOW RATE IS NOT AS HIGH AS EARLIER, HOWEVER THE OVERFLOW IS STILL ONGOING BUT ONLY TRICKLING. EED-ACT 2019/08/18 AT 08H17. J

THERE WAS VERY FAINT, BARELY NOTICEABLE LIGHTER SHEEN IN THE SCENE THAT HAD DIFFUSE EDGES, THEREFORE ITS TRUE EXTENT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED. UNCERTAINTIES: ALTHOUGH THE SLICK WAS THOUGHT TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH A REPEAT POINT SOURCE, THE SOURCE COULD NOT BE DETERMINED BECAUSE OF CLOUD COVER OR OTHER FACTORS, SUCH AS THE TERMINATION OF THE SCENE. ADDITIONALLY, THE SLICK WAS VERY DIFFUSE ON ITS SOUTHERN EDGE, RENDERING ITS TRUE EXTENT INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ITS SURROUNDINGS. THE BARGE WAS LEFT ALONG THE SHORE ON FRIDAY AS A PRECAUTION WITH ABSORBENT BOOM ALONGSIDE. AT THAT TIME THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF A RELEASE AND THE BARGE WAS SITTING ON THE BOTTOM. THE HOSES ARE ALSO TOO SHORT AND WOULD NOT HAVE ENOUGH PRESSURE FOR FIRE-FIGHTING AT THE LOCATION. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT IS THUS FORCED TO ALLOW THE VEHICLE TO BURN.

KOLARIK HAD AGREED WITH THE CONDO ASSOCIATION'S REQUIREMENT THAT SHE TEST FOR HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES PRIOR TO REMOVAL, BUT SHE DID NOT DO THIS. THIS WAS THE SECOND INSTANCE OF DUST BEING GENERATED. THE LOCAL POLICE AND BOARD OF HEALTH COULD NOT TAKE ACTION WERE NOTIFIED BUT COULD NOT TAKE ACTION.

UNCERTAINTIES: THE EXACT SOURCE OF THE ANOMALY COULD NOT BE IDENTIFIED, AS MULTIPLE FACILITIES WERE LOCATED IN THE VICINITY. ADDITIONALLY, THE IMAGE WAS CUT OFF TO THE WEST OF THE ANOMALY, AND AS A RESULT, THE FULL EXTENT MAY NOT HAVE BEEN CAPTURED IN THIS REPORT.

Report Description/// THIS IS A 48 HR PHMSA UPDATE TO NRC REPORT # 1362513 /// UPDATED INFO IS AS FOLLOWS: - INITIAL INCIDENT INVESTIGATION INDICATED THAT A 2 INCH POLY GAS LINE WAS CROSS BORED WITH THE SEWER LATERAL WHEN IT WAS INSTALLED. - ON THE TOPSIDE OF GAS LINE WITHIN THE WIDTH OF THE SEWER LATERAL, A SMALL HOLE WAS DISCOVERED IN THE GAS LINE. - TIMING OF THE LEAK COINCIDE WITH 3RD PARTY PLUMBING ACTIVITIES IN THE SEWER LATERAL. - INVESTIGATION CONTINUES AND WILL INCLUDE LABORATORY ANALYSIS OF THE DAMAGED GAS PIPE. - LEAK SURVEY WERE PERFORMED SEVERAL TIMES OVER THE LAST 2 DAYS AND NO ADDITIONAL LEAKS WERE FOUND. - THE GAS MAIN WAS PRESSURE TESTED IN THE AREA AND IT HELD THE PRESSURE. - METER DATA WAS REVIEWED FOR THE RESIDENCE AND NO SPIKE AND USAGES WERE DETECTED. - ADDITIONAL INFORMATION WILL BE PROVIDED IN THE 30 DAYS PHMSA REPORT. - RELEASE WAS SECURED AT 2206 ON 17MARCH. INITIAL REPORT: THE CALLER STATES A FIRE WITH EXPLOSION AT A PRIVATE RESIDENCE. 3 CITIZEN WERE TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL. NO EVACUATIONS AT THIS TIME. LOCAL NEWS IS ON SITE.

Report Description/// 48HR PHMSA UPDATE TO INCIDENT REPORT # 1418351 /// UPDATE IS AS FOLLOWS: THE CALLER STATES THAT THEY ARE THE SUSPECTED RESPONSIBLE PARTY FOR THIS INCIDENT. THE CALLER STATES THAT THE VEHICLE INVOLVED WAS A TANKER TRUCK AND TANKER TRAILER THAT SLID ON THE ICY ROAD. THE CALLER STATES THAT THE TANKER TRUCK HIT A JERSEY BARRIER, WITH NO RELEASE OF MATERIALS, BUT THE TANKER TRAILER DETACHED AND ROLLED INTO A NEARBY DRY DITCH, RELEASING 3602 GALLONS OF GASOLINE ONTO SOIL. LOCAL FIRST RESPONDERS, AND MULTIPLE AGENCIES, ARRIVED ON SCENE TO SECURE THE RELEASE FROM THE TRAILER, AND CONDUCT AN INVESTIGATION. THE CALLER STATES THAT HEAVY EQUIPMENT ARRIVED ONSCENE TO REMOVE THE TANKER TRAILER FROM THE DITCH, AND TOW BOTH THE TANKER TRUCK AND TANKER TRAILER. ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION IS AS FOLLOWS: THE CALLER STATED THAT A TANKER TRUCK SLID ON ICE AND TURNED OVER. BECAUSE OF THIS (1500) GALLONS OF GASOLINE RELEASED ONTO SOIL AND A STORM DRAIN AT THE LOCATION. THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES, FATALITIES, OR ROAD CLOSURES IN CONNECTION TO THIS INCIDENT.

STAFF PUT SPILL TRAY UNDER VAC TRUCK, STARTED RECOVERING WATER FROM ROADWAY AS WELL CB WAS OPENED AND RESIDUAL WATER WAS PUMPED OUT OF THE CB. CALLER CONFIRMED SOME EXITED THE CB OUT INTO PORT HOPE HARBOUR CALLER REPORTS THE SITE HAD RECENTLY DEMOLISHED A FORMER PRODUCTION FACILITY BLDG THEY HAVE BEEN COLLECTING WATER FROM THE SLAB OF THE STRUCTURE AND PUMPING INTO FRAC TANK THEY HAD A WASTE HAULER ON SITE TODAY - GFL WHEN CONTRACTOR VAC TRUCK BEGAN TO PUMP WATER FROM STORAGE TANK TO THE VAC TRUCK. THE VAC TRUCK ITSELF WAS LEAKING DURING THE TRANSFER. IT WAS DETERMINED THE HATCH ON THE TRUCK WAS LEAKING THE WATER VACUUMED INTO THE VAC TRUCK WAS DISCHARGING THROUGH THE BACK OF THE TRUCK AND WAS GOING INTO THE MUNICIPAL CB. CALLER REPORTS WILL NOTIFY THE MUNICIPALITY NEXT.
